speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) in each of the past five years, how many migrant domestic workers and unofficial employers have been fined for illegal moonlighting; and (b) what is the take-up rate of the Household Services Scheme since its permanent formalisation in 2021.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Based on surveys, the number of households served by HSS companies have also increased steadily.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: A recent straw poll amongst our female union leaders also highlighted the lack of options for affordable caregiving and housekeeping support for working families.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Could the Ministry look to expanding the HSS to beyond its current operators to increase service options or to make more accessible the booking of such part-time, caregiving or housekeeping services through online means?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: And would the Ministry look perhaps to what was the union on strengthening public awareness on existing schemes like the HSS, as there seems to be a limited understanding on the scheme even with our female union leaders?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Indeed, there are a range of caregiving and housekeeping options for households, depending on their needs.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: All companies interested in joining an HSS scheme can write to MOM.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: The number of companies have increased, like I mentioned, from 80 to 240.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: We leave it to companies to reach out for their bookings.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: And should there be any interest of these companies, they can also offer online booking services at the convenience of their clients.
